pages.content:
<callout icon="✅" color="green_bg">
Built 3 October 2026 — 31 tests passing. Tenancy, auth, roles, plan limits, the catalogue and batch model, the sale path, and Ghana's compliance records are implemented and runnable. No dependencies: Node 24 runs the TypeScript directly and ships its own SQLite.
</callout>

## What exists now

**Schema** (`db/schema.sql`, portable across SQLite and PostgreSQL): plans · tenants · subscriptions · branches · users · sessions · categories · products · suppliers · batches · stock_movements · purchases · purchase_items · customers · prescriptions · sales · sale_items · payments · controlled_register · audit_log.

**Modules**

- `tenant.ts` — the isolation layer every read and write passes through
- `auth.ts` — registration, login, sessions, staff accounts
- `permissions.ts` — the role matrix
- `plans.ts` — tiers and limit enforcement
- `catalog.ts` — products, suppliers, branches, batch receiving, expiry, reorder
- `sales.ts` — the counter: first-expiry-first-out, payments, movements, controlled dispensing
- `prescriptions.ts` — prescriptions with the two-year retention window
- `controlled.ts` — the Controlled Drugs Register
- `reports.ts` — asset values, sales summary, top products
- `audit.ts` — the audit trail

## The two decisions, answered

**Offline — online-only for the pilot, UUID keys from day one.** Sales go straight to the server. Primary keys are UUIDs anyway, so an offline queue can be added later without migrating a single key.

**Regulatory — the register is required, so it is in v1.** The Pharmacy Act 1994 (Act 489) s.34 requires anyone supplying Class A or B drugs to keep a Dangerous Drugs Record showing the drug and quantity, the name and address of the person supplied, the signature of the person supplying, and the date of supply. s.32 requires a dispensed prescription to be retained on the premises for two years. The FDA's controlled drugs guideline (FDA/DRI/TSA/GL-SSCS/2020/07 §4.3.1) requires a Controlled Drugs Register for everything obtained and supplied, kept and available for inspection for at least two years, and restricts pharmacy supply to a valid prescription or signed order. So the register is append-only, prescriptions carry a `retained_until` date, and controlled or prescription-only items cannot be sold without one.

Sources: [Pharmacy Act 1994 (Act 489)](https://www.moh.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Pharmacy-Act-1994-Act-489.pdf) · [FDA — sale, supply and use of controlled drugs](https://fdaghana.gov.gh/final-guidelines-for-the-sale-supply-and-use-of-controlled-drugs-4/) · [Pharmacy Council of Ghana](https://pcghana.org/)

## Rules the code enforces

| Rule | Where |
| --- | --- |
| A tenant can only ever read its own rows | `tenant.ts` |
| Stock is drawn first-expiry-first-out | `sales.ts` |
| Expired batches can never be supplied | `sales.ts`, `catalog.ts` |
| Controlled drugs need a prescription | `sales.ts` |
| Only owner or administrator may dispense a controlled drug | `permissions.ts` |
| Asset values are owner-only | `permissions.ts`, `reports.ts` |
| Plan limits block an over-limit action | `plans.ts` |
| Every quantity change writes a stock movement | `catalog.ts`, `sales.ts` |
| Every mutation writes an audit row | `audit.ts` |

## Tests

31 passing: 6 isolation, 8 auth, 10 sales, 7 compliance. Run with `npm test`.

The suite caught two real problems while I was building it:

- **A parameter-ordering bug in the isolation layer.** A query that filtered the tenant inside a JOIN ordered its placeholders differently from one that filtered in WHERE, so the positional tenant binding read the wrong column and the query returned nothing. The scope now binds the tenant by an explicit `{{tenant}}` marker and refuses any query that does not carry exactly one.
- **My own arithmetic in a test**, not the code: safe plus non-perishable assets were 9,000 pesewas, not 12,000. The code was right.

## Run it

```bash
npm test      # 31 tests
npm run seed  # demo pharmacy, one day of trading
```

The seed prints a day of trading, asset values, expiry and reorder alerts, and the Controlled Drugs Register as an inspector would read it:

```
walk-in sale             GHS 27.50  change GHS 22.50
prescription sale       GHS 150.00  (3 lines)
controlled dispense      GHS 50.00  register entries: 1

--- asset values (owner only) ---
total                  GHS 3857.50
lost (expired)          GHS 120.00

--- Controlled Drugs Register (as an inspector reads it) ---
  2026-10-03  received  Pethidine    PET-01   qty  20  from supplier
  2026-10-03  supplied  Pethidine    PET-01   qty   2  Kwame Boateng — 12 Ring Road, Accra
              supplied by Emmanuel Lartey, signature ref (captured on the printed register)
```

## The code

<file source="session-file://fcafb06d-d3ae-4632-8cff-7f4f79b9de22" />

rxpos-m1.zip

Git history starts with a single commit, and `npm test` runs with no install step.

## Still open

- CI and a deploy target, and no git remote yet.
- The counter UI — the prototype is still the visual reference — and thermal receipt printing.
- Paystack and mobile money are recorded, not charged.
- Purchases exist in the schema and on the receipt path, but there is no ordering flow.
- Email is globally unique, so one login cannot yet belong to two pharmacies.
- The Dangerous Drugs Record is stored electronically. Whether an inspector accepts a printed electronic register or expects the physical book is worth confirming with the Pharmacy Council before the pilot.
